title: Component reference hub: canonical usage guides, migration lanes, and API shim examples for tokens/buttons/tables/charts
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: Create a single, practical reference page per surface (Tokens, Buttons, Tables, Charts) that contains: concise usage guidance (when to use X vs Y), code-first examples for our React and REST clients, clear do/don't callouts, and a short migration lane with mapping notes and lightweight API shims developers can drop in to reduce churn.

Scope: four canonical reference documents (one per surface) delivered as markdown-based pages in the docsite. Each reference page will include:
- Quick decision tree (1–2 questions) to pick the right primitive/variant.
- Minimal examples: React JSX + plain HTML/CSS snippets + pseudo-API for non-JS clients.
- Accessibility checklist and common testing assertions (keyboard, focus, color contrast).
- Migration lane: checklist, legacy-to-new token mappings, and an opt-in compatibility shim for 1 release cycle.
- QA notes and rollout plan for deprecations.

Why this work: Engineering continues to raise questions about ambiguous token usage (raw colors vs semantic token), inconsistent button variants across apps, and subtle table behaviors (virtualization vs pagination). The docsite needs compact, actionable guidance so teams can reason about trade-offs quickly and adopt the new tokens/components without bespoke design hand-holding.

Principles to follow in content: prioritize low cognitive overhead, prefer code examples over long prose, and make migration steps reversible and timeboxed (1 release). Avoid prescribing implementation details that lock runtime constraints (e.g., don’t require a specific virtualization lib).

Highlights (surface-level guidance):
- Tokens: always prefer semantic tokens (color.surface.* / color.text.* / space.*) in component styles. Use raw token values only in one-off utility CSS in apps that require overrides. Document the mapping table for legacy tokens (legacy-blue-500 -> color.primary.default) and provide a small CSS variables shim to map legacy names to new tokens at runtime.
- Buttons: encourage three high-level intents (primary, neutral, ghost) and two density sizes (regular, compact). Use explicit state tokens (button.background.hover, button.border.focus) instead of color arithmetic in component code. Demonstrate how to use the Button API props (variant, size, tone, disabled) with examples for icon-only and loading states.
- Tables: recommend 'density' prop for row height and a small API surface: columns definition, rowKey, virtualization boolean, and stickyHeader boolean. Provide patterns for sorting, selection and server-driven pagination. Callout: prefer server-side pagination for >5k rows; prefer virtualization for interactive viewport lists.
- Charts: document semantic color palettes for data vs decorative elements, accessibility recommendations for colorblind-friendly palettes, and guidance on chart labeling and summaries for screen readers. Include a small code snippet showing how to export chart image and provide alt text fallback.

Migration notes (pragmatic lane):
- Step 1: Instrument: add telemetry key to legacy components to detect usage (2 weeks).
- Step 2: Add compatibility CSS variables shim in app root that maps legacy tokens to semantic tokens (example provided).
- Step 3: Replace internal component references to semantic tokens; publish minor release with backward compat flags.
- Step 4: Start deprecation notices in console and docs; schedule removal window (1 release after grace period).

Acceptance tests (high level):
- Each reference page has at least one runnable example in docsite's code sandbox (React) and a plain HTML file.
- Migration shim snippet validated against two customer apps (internal staging).
- Accessibility checklist items validated by Design QA and recorded in page metadata.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Compatibility shims increase short-term maintenance; mitigate by timeboxing to one release cycle and providing telemetry.
- Overstuffed pages: keep examples minimal and link to deeper how-to guides rather than expanding the single reference page.

Rollout plan: Draft pages -> Design review -> Engineering review and small PoC in one internal app -> Publish behind 'beta' toggle on docsite -> Monitor telemetry -> Flip default and announce.

Expected outcome: a compact, developer-friendly docset that reduces ambiguous questions in PR reviews and speeds up migration to semantic tokens and standardized components.
acceptance_criteria: Four reference pages delivered: Tokens, Buttons, Tables, Charts
Each page contains a decision tree, code examples (React + plain HTML), and accessibility checklist
Migration lane documented with a CSS variables shim example and a removal timeline
Design and Engineering reviews completed and recorded in comments
One internal app uses the shim and verifies no visual regressions
